rv.q: Hytner's updated production gives each character sharp definition and turns one of Shakespeare's least treasured works into a powerful comment on the insulating effect of wealth and the precariousness of a credit culture in which reality is kept at bay.
Simon Russell Beale is a masterful Timon, all back-slapping bonhomie at the start but fearsome in the depths of his misanthropic misery.
What looks to be a surprise domestic hit will be exported via worldwide live broadcast screenings on Nov. 1.

cn.t: Hytner's bold, topical production makes Shakespeare's rarely-staged parable about money and betrayal feel urgently relevant. Critics praise its striking visuals and compelling central performance in this caustic, exhilarating staging.
